sources.citation: Palmer, Edward. 1886. No. 111 Akoonkoon, Palmer River. In E.M. Curr (ed.), The Australian Race, vol. II, 396-399. Melbourne: Government Printer.
sources.note: Wordlist of the 'Mirkin tribe' (country from Palmerville to the Palmer-Mitchell junction) in Curr's English-based orthography, ~100 items plus a short ethnographic note; no stress marking or pronunciation remarks. sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Kokomini' (raw wikitext, 2026), quoting Breen, Gavan 2016, 'WE Roth and the study of Aboriginal languages in Queensland', in McDougall & Davidson (eds), The Roth Family, Anthropology, and Colonial Administration, p. 144.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Second-hand: Roth's 1899 Koko-minni report appends wordlists of four languages, the first from the 'Koko-minni Chief Camp: head of Annie Creek and King River'; Sommer (1976:133) calls Koko-Minni ('speech-good'/'speech intelligible') a 'loose confederation' of dialects or even separate languages; Rigsby (p.c. to Breen) equates Roth's Koko-Minni with Palmer's 1884 Akoonkoon/Akoonkol and Koogobatha; Tindale 1974:176 places the Kokomini on the middle Palmer and Mitchell rivers.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2013. Change Request 2013-030: retire [ggm] Gugu Mini (adopted 2014-02-03). SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States 'Gugu Mini' is apparently a generic term meaning 'good speech' used for several languages in the Thaypan area; quotes AIATSIS Y94 entry (Rigsby 2005:138: reference shifting, variable, wide-ranging; Sommer 2008 p.c.: Kuku Mini = 'speech good', Central Paman type; map location from Tindale 1974 'Kokomini'); AIATSIS status 'potential data' (wordlists only); name absent from Bowern's 2012 master list.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2012. Change Request 2012-138: split [ggr] Aghu Tharnggalu into [gtu], [ggm], [ikr] (adopted 2013-01-23).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Ethnologue had listed 'Kuku-Mini' as an alternate name of Aghu Tharnggalu; AUSTLANG tentatively lists Gugu Mini as a language while noting it may be a cover term; Gugu Mini and Aghu-Tharnggala treated as separate in Wurm 1972/1994, Oates 1975, Walsh 1981, Bowern 2011 centroid map.

sources.citation: Wikipedia articles 'Ikarranggal language', 'Aghu Tharrnggala language', 'Gugu Thaypan language'; Glottolog aghu1254 and kunj1245 pages; Pama Language Centre 'Uw Oykangand linguistic notes and sources'; D. Nash's K.L. Hale Australian bibliography.
sources.note: Nothing on stress for Gugu Mini. Ikarranggal and Aghu Tharrnggala are each said to be 'often referred to as Gogo Mini (Kuku-Mini) good speech'; Aghu Tharrnggala's Wikipedia phonology (from Jolly 1989) gives segments only. Pama Centre page: Sommer 2006:7 lists Koko-minni among the Kunjen group. Nash's Hale bibliography: Hale 1960 'Other Paman languages' ms (AIATSIS pMS 741/742) Proto-Paman list uses forms from 'Kuku Mini (or Ogo NdYan)', i.e. equates Kuku Mini with Ogh Undjan.
